captions.instagram:
How does a cinema projector work?

A Maltese cross that stops the film 24 times a second, a shutter that flashes every frame twice, and a chip with 9 million tilting mirrors. Step into the booth and see how a cinema throws a picture 30 metres onto a wall.

→ A film projector pulls each frame into the gate, holds it still, and flashes light through it.
→ A Maltese cross turns a quarter turn per frame: the film jumps down, then stands still.
→ Two shutter blades flash every frame twice: 24 frames become 48 flashes, too fast to see flicker.
→ A digital projector splits light into red, green and blue, one mirror chip for each.
→ Each pixel is a mirror that tilts ±12°, flipping thousands of times a second to make grey.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/projectorclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a cinema projector work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A Maltese cross that stops the film 24 times a second, a shutter that flashes every frame twice, and a chip with 9 million tilting mirrors. Step into the booth and see how a cinema throws a picture 30 metres onto a wall.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/projectorclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/projectorclear

In this video:
• Film stops, flashes, then jumps. A 35 mm projector pulls film from a platter through a gate.
• Nine million mirrors per colour. A digital cinema projector splits lamp or laser light into red, green and blue, one DLP chip each.
• The lens sets the size, the screen sets the brightness. Picture width = throw × chip width ÷ focal length.
• 3D is two films sharing one screen. One projector flashes left and right pictures 144 times a second.
• A film in files, locked with a key. Films arrive as a DCP: JPEG 2000 frames at up to 250 Mbit/s, roughly 150 to 250 GB for a feature, by drive, internet or satellite (India's UFO Moviez and Qube pioneered satellite delivery).
• Bigger, faster, brighter. IMAX runs 70 mm film sideways, 15 perforations a frame, about ten times the area of 35 mm, and now uses twin lasers.
